## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. You are re-implementing a C++ URL parser program in pure Rust (std only, edition 2021). The reference C++ binary is at /workspace/dataset/test16_executable (run it with one URL argument to see expected output). Create a complete Cargo project in /output.

## Required structure
- `/output/Cargo.toml` — package, edition = "2021", plus `[[bin]] name = "test16", path = "test16.rs"` so `cargo build --release` produces `target/release/test16`.
- `/output/url_parser.rs` — the library module (struct `URL` with methods `scheme()`, `host()`, `port()`, `path()`; free functions `is_valid_url`, `is_scheme_valid`, `is_host_valid`, `is_port_valid`, `split_path`). If you want multiple modules, use `/output/url_parser/mod.rs` style so plain `rustc` still works.
- `/output/test16.rs` — entry file in package root, starts with `mod url_parser;` so BOTH `cargo build --release` AND `rustc --edition 2021 -O test16.rs -o test16` (run in /output) work.

## Exact behavior (inferred by black-box probing of the C++ binary; match it exactly)

main: collect `std::env::args()`. If fewer than 2 args, exit with code 1 printing nothing. Otherwise url = args[1], print (each on its own line, `\n`-terminated):
1. `is_valid_url(url)` as `1`/`0`
2. `is_scheme_valid(parser.scheme())` as `1`/`0`
3. `is_host_valid(parser.host())` as `1`/`0`
4. `is_port_valid(parser.port())` as `1`/`0`
5. number of path segments (from `split_path(parser.path())`)
6. each segment on its own line, verbatim

Parsing algorithm for `URL::new(url)`:
1. If url contains the substring `://` (FIRST occurrence, byte search): scheme = part before it, rest = part after. Else scheme = "", rest = whole url.
2. Cut rest at the EARLIEST of the first `?` or first `#` (whichever index is smaller); drop everything from there.
3. Split rest at the first `/`: authority = before it, path = from the `/` onward (INCLUDING the leading `/`). If no `/`: authority = rest, path = "".
4. If authority contains `@` (first occurrence): hostport = part after it; else hostport = authority. (userinfo discarded)
5. If hostport contains `:` (first occurrence): host = before, port = after; else host = hostport, port = "".

Validation functions:
- `is_scheme_valid(s)`: s non-empty; first char ASCII alphabetic; every remaining char ASCII alphanumeric or one of `+`, `-`, `.`.
- `is_host_valid(h)`: h non-empty; every BYTE is ASCII alphanumeric or one of `.`, `-`, `[`, `]`. (Everything else — space, tab, `_`, `~`, `%`, `!`, `@`, `&`, non-ASCII like `é` — is invalid.)
- `is_port_valid(p)`: emulate C++ `std::stoi` then range check: skip leading C-locale whitespace (space, \t, \n, \v, \f, \r); optional `+` or `-`; require at least one ASCII digit (else false); parse the digit prefix only (trailing junk ignored, e.g. "80abc" → 80, "0x50" → 0); if the value overflows i32 (e.g. "99999999999999999999") → false; valid iff 0 <= value <= 65535. Examples: "" → false, "abc" → false, "-1" → false, "65535" → true, "65536" → false, "+80" → true, " 80" → true, "80 " → true, "-0" → true, ":"-produced empty → false.
- `is_valid_url(u)` = parsed host non-empty OR parsed path non-empty. (E.g. "" → 0, "http://" → 0, "http://?q=1" → 0, "?q" → 0, "http:///" → 1, "a" → 1, " " → 1.)
- `split_path(p)`: split p on `/`, keep only non-empty segments, verbatim (a segment of a single space IS kept).

Handle non-ASCII input bytes safely (operate on bytes internally or only slice at ASCII-delimiter boundaries so no panic on UTF-8 input like `http://éxample.com`).

## Verification before you finish
Build both ways (`cargo build --release` in /output, and `rustc --edition 2021 -O test16.rs -o /output/test16` in /output). Then run this probe set against BOTH /workspace/dataset/test16_executable and your binary and confirm byte-identical output for every input:
"http://example.com" "https://localhost:8080" "example.com" "http://" "" "://x" "http://exa mple.com" "http://example.com:65536" "http://example.com:0x50" "http://example.com:99999999999999999999" "http://example.com:80abc" "http://user:80@example.com" "http://a@b@c.com:xx" "http://example.com:xx:90" "http://[::1]:8080" "h_ttp://x.com" "ht+tp://x.com" "http://example.com/a//b" "http://example.com/a/ /b" "http://example.com/path?query=1" "example.com/a#b/c" "mailto:user@example.com" "file:///etc/passwd" "http:/example.com" "http://a://b" "?q" "#f" "http://example.com:-0" "http://éxample.com" "http://ho[st" "http://ho]st" "http://ho&st" " " "http:///"
Report: files created, build results, and whether all probes matched. Do NOT modify anything under /workspace.
